questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements concerning the duties of the appropriate Government under the RTE Act:
I. It must provide free and compulsory elementary education to every child.
II. It must ensure the availability of a neighbourhood school within a specified period.
III. It must provide private tuitions to children lagging in academics. Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Statements I and II are correct. Sections 6 and 8 place obligations on the appropriate Government and local authorities to ensure free and compulsory elementary education and to make neighbourhood-school access available within the prescribed period. Statement III is incorrect: the Act does not impose a general obligation to provide private tuition to children who are academically behind. The statutory approach is to ensure access and appropriate learning support within the education system.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर I और II है। RTE अधिनियम समुचित सरकार और स्थानीय प्राधिकारियों पर निःशुल्क तथा अनिवार्य प्रारंभिक शिक्षा उपलब्ध कराने और आवश्यक विद्यालयी पहुँच सुनिश्चित करने का दायित्व रखता है। अधिनियम यह सामान्य दायित्व नहीं देता कि सरकार प्रत्येक शैक्षणिक रूप से पीछे रह गए बच्चे के लिए निजी ट्यूशन की व्यवस्था करे। ऐसे बच्चों के लिए उपयुक्त शैक्षिक सहायता और विशेष प्रशिक्षण के प्रावधान अलग संदर्भ में लागू होते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Statements I and II are correct. Sections 6 and 8 place obligations on the appropriate Government and local authorities to ensure free and compulsory elementary education and to make neighbourhood-school access available within the prescribed period. Statement III is incorrect: the Act does not impose a general obligation to provide private tuition to children who are academically behind. The statutory approach is to ensure access and appropriate learning support within the education system.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) 2

questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps in the RTE Act grievance-redressal mechanism:
I. Complaint to the Local Authority.
II. Appeal to the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR).
III. Decision by the Local Authority within three months.
IV. Grievance raised by a parent or guardian. Which sequence is correct?
options_english: IV, I, III, II
IV, III, I, II
I, IV, II, III
IV, II, I, III
questions.explanation_english: The correct sequence is IV, I, III, II. questions.question_english: Under the RTE Act, "screening procedure" is explicitly defined as:
options_english: Selecting a child for admission in preference to another by non-random methods.
Conducting a routine physical health assessment checking the child's vision and hearing.
Formally verifying the official local residential address and domicile of the child.
Inspecting and validating the official medical immunization records of the applicant child.
questions.explanation_english: Section 2(o) defines a "screening procedure" as any method of selection for admitting a child that relies on non-random criteria, including competitive entry tests, academic evaluations, or parental interviews, rather than open, non- discriminatory random selection methods.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। RTE अधिनियम में स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया का अर्थ प्रवेश के लिए एक बच्चे को दूसरे पर गैर-यादृच्छिक तरीके से प्राथमिकता देना है। नियमित स्वास्थ्य-जाँच, आवासीय पते का प्रशासनिक सत्यापन या टीकाकरण अभिलेख देखना अपने आप में वही स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया नहीं है। धारा 13 का उद्देश्य प्रवेश को चयन-परीक्षा, साक्षात्कार या अन्य भेदभावपूर्ण चयन विधियों से मुक्त रखना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Selecting a child for admission in preference to another by non-random methods.

questions.question_english: Under Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, what percentage of the total strength of Class I must be filled by children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in a private unaided school?
options_english: At least 15%
At least 20%
At least 25%
At least 30%
questions.explanation_english: Section 12(1)(c) mandates that private unaided non-minority schools must reserve at least twenty-five percent of their entry-level seats, such as Class 1 or pre-school, for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups. These students must be provided free elementary education, with schools receiving state reimbursement equivalent to per-child government expenditure.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर 25% है। धारा 12(1)(ग) निर्दिष्ट निजी गैर-सहायता-प्राप्त और निर्दिष्ट श्रेणी के विद्यालयों में प्रवेश-स्तर पर कमजोर वर्गों और वंचित समूहों के बच्चों के लिए कम-से-कम 25 प्रतिशत सीटों का प्रावधान करती है। यह प्रावधान सामाजिक समावेशन और शिक्षा तक समान पहुँच को बढ़ावा देने के लिए बनाया गया है। इसे सभी कक्षाओं की कुल सीटों पर लागू होने वाले सामान्य आरक्षण के रूप में नहीं पढ़ना चाहिए; प्रश्न प्रवेश-स्तर की कक्षा I सीटों की बात करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) At least 25%

Section 12(1)(c) mandates that private unaided non-minority schools must reserve at least twenty-five percent of their entry-level seats, such as Class 1 or pre-school, for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups. These students must be provided free elementary education, with schools receiving state reimbursement equivalent to per-child government expenditure.

questions.question_english: Section 4 of the RTE Act provides for "Special Training". Who is the primary target group for this provision?
options_english: Out-of-school or non-enrolled children above six years of age.
Academically gifted children requiring specialized advanced coaching modules.
In-service regular teachers who currently lack minimum NCTE professional qualifications.
Students preparing for competitive secondary level school entrance examinations.
questions.explanation_english: Section 4 targets out-of-school children—those who have never been enrolled or dropped out early—who are above six years of age. The provision mandates admitting them to age- appropriate classes and providing specialized training to help them achieve class-appropriate learning levels alongside their peers seamlessly.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विद्यालय से बाहर या नामांकित न हुए बच्चे हैं। धारा 4 उन बच्चों के लिए विशेष प्रशिक्षण की व्यवस्था करती है जो कभी विद्यालय नहीं गए या प्रारंभिक शिक्षा पूरी नहीं कर पाए। उन्हें आयु-उपयुक्त कक्षा में प्रवेश दिया जाता है और उनकी सीखने की कमी दूर करने के लिए विशेष प्रशिक्षण उपलब्ध कराया जाता है। यह प्रावधान प्रतिभाशाली बच्चों की उन्नत कोचिंग या शिक्षकों के व्यावसायिक प्रशिक्षण के लिए नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Out-of-school or non-enrolled children above six years of age.

questions.question_english: For a school to be recognized, the RTE Act requires a library. The schedule specifically mandates that the library must provide:

A minimum inventory of at least 500 reference books focused exclusively on science and mathematics.

questions.question_english: As a Principal establishing an SMC in a new government school, you invite local residents, parents, and a local authority representative. The total SMC membership is fixed at 16. What is the minimum number of women members and parent members required?
options_english: 8 women members and 12 parent members
8 women members and 8 parent members
5 women members and 10 parent members

questions.explanation_english: Statutory rules mandate that at least 75% of SMC members must be parents/guardians, and at least 50% must be women. For a 16-member SMC, 75% equals twelve parent members, and 50% equals eight women members, satisfying both legal minimum thresholds for community representation and gender inclusion.
